verses.author: model_A
verses.text: My grandmother's hands remember a language I never learned.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Frost writes on the window overnight—
by morning someone else's fingerprint
has already melted it away.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Steam rises from the pot on the stove,
carrying no words at all,
and still I know it means *sit down, eat*.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I keep a spoon she never touched
and call it inheritance—
the shape of a hand still fits the handle.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Rain finds the gutter it has always known,
runs the same crooked path down the drive—
no one taught the water where to go.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The dog waits at a door I've already closed,
nose against the crack of light—
some habits outlive the reason for them.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The porch light burns through breakfast, noon, and dusk—
nobody left to flick the switch,
so it just keeps calling the moths home.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I count the jars still sealed in the pantry,
each lid a small held breath—
some things we save just to prove we haven't lost everything yet.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The kettle knows the hour without a clock,
sings out at four though no one's listening—
old songs don't need an audience to keep singing.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I fold the letter back along its worn crease,
not to read it, just to feel
paper remember the shape of being needed.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The dog still waits by the gate at five,
ears up for a truck that changed its route years ago—
hope doesn't check the calendar before it starts.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I leave the porch light burning past midnight,
not for anyone walking home—
just so the dark has one thing it can't have.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Frost writes its own name on the window glass,
gone by nine, no one to read it—
some things sign themselves and disappear anyway.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I keep a jar of buttons with no coats,
each one a small full stop
to shirts that finished their sentences long ago.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The kettle clicks off though no one poured the water—
some habits keep working
after the reason for them walks out the door.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I count the change in my pocket without spending it,
just to feel it add up to something—
some hands need a small math they can win.
